payout_quote: NAUPA on unclaimed.org: 'Yes! It is free to search for and claim your missing money! There is no fee to search for and claim your unclaimed property — if you use your official state program.' This finds money ALREADY OWED TO YOU (a forgotten account, uncashed check, security deposit) if it exists in a state database — it never promises anyone has any.
timing: Search is instant. Claim processing is handled by each state's official program — typically weeks to a few months after you submit proof of identity and ownership.
biggest_catch: This finds YOUR OWN money only if it exists in a state database — most searches return nothing, and that is the normal result. You must claim through the official state program; third-party 'finder' services take a cut of your money for something you can do yourself for free.
eligibility: Anyone who has lived or done business in a US state, province, or territory. To claim a match you must prove your identity and ownership (e.g., SSN, utility bill, pay stub, old address).
steps: Go to https://unclaimed.org/search/ and use the interactive map to pick your state, or use MissingMoney.com (the free multi-state search sponsored by NAUPA) to check participating states at once.
Search EVERY state you have lived or done business in — property is reported to the state where the company resides, so matches commonly span multiple states.
If your name matches, click through to that state's official unclaimed-property program website (never a third-party finder).
File the claim on the state site and upload proof of identity and ownership (pay stub, utility bill, SSN, old address records).
Track the claim on the state site; expect weeks to a few months for verification and payout.
catches: Most searches return nothing — NAUPA says 1 in 10 people have unclaimed property, which means 9 in 10 do not.
Third-party 'finder' firms may legally take a percentage of your money; the official state program is always free — use it directly.
You must prove ownership with documents (SSN, old addresses, pay stubs, utility bills); a name match alone pays nothing.
Impostor sites mimic state programs — always reach the state site from unclaimed.org's map or MissingMoney.com.
Claims are verified by the state before payout, so even a confirmed match takes weeks to months.

NAUPA is the official association of state unclaimed-property administrators; the site routes users to official state programs and sponsors MissingMoney.com. In-app, this route must push users ONLY to official state sites and warn against fee-charging finders. No app exists — website only.
